title: Homepage hero: technical assurances and fallback experiments
content:
OVERVIEW:
This is a compact messaging brief + experiment plan for adding technical reassurance and graceful-degradation/fallback language to the homepage hero and product blurbs. Goal is to test whether explicit operational assurances (latency SLOs, fallback model paths, private deployment options) improve trial conversion for engineering buyers without alienating product/PM audiences who prioritize simplicity.

GOALS (primary):
- Increase API trial activation rate for teams evaluating production inference (measured as signups that test inference within 7 days).
- Reduce mid-funnel bounce on product pages (time on page and click-to-try).
- Collect qualitative feedback from pilot accounts on whether fallback assurances are decision-relevant.

TARGET AUDIENCES (primary to secondary):
- Platform/ML engineers evaluating inference runtime (care about latency, determinism, model controls).
- Backend engineers / infra leads (care about SLA, isolation, VPC).
- Product engineers / PMs (care about time-to-value and cost predictability).
- CTO/VP Eng (enterprise purchase triggers: compliance, auditability).

PRINCIPAL MESSAGE PILLARS (to weave into hero and supporting copy):
1) Predictable performance: "Engineered for production latency and throughput — configurable SLOs and dedicated capacity."
2) Cost control: "Options to optimize per-token unit economics with batching, quantization, and routing policies."
3) Reliability & graceful degradation: "Automated fallbacks and model routing keep apps online under load."
4) Deployment flexibility: "Hosted, reserved dedicated pools, or private VPC/on-prem with customer key control."
5) Observability: "Token-level breakdowns, per-route tracing, and regression alerts."

WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT:
- Existing homepage variants focus heavily on speed/cost/value hooks. We hypothesize a sizable segment of engineering evaluators drop out because they don't see operational guarantees up front. Adding compact, explicit assurances (one-liners + micro bullets) may bridge that gap without adding complexity.

HERO COPY VARIANTS (3 short experiments)
Variant A — "Production-first inference. Ship faster, keep costs down."
- Subhead: "Predictable latency and cost controls for teams running LLMs in production. Hosted, dedicated, or private."
- Micro-CTA: "Start a free inference test"
- Technical micro-strip under CTA (smaller font, one line): "SLOs, model fallbacks, and per-token tracing out of the box."

Variant B — "Keep your app online when traffic spikes."
- Subhead: "Automatic model routing + dedicated pools ensure low latency and smooth degradation."
- Micro-CTA: "Run a synthetic load"
- Technical micro-strip: "Fallbacks to compatible variants, region-aware routing, and burst capacity."

Variant C — "Control cost, control quality, control deployment."
- Subhead: "Transparent unit economics + model governance for production teams."
- Micro-CTA: "See a cost demo"
- Technical micro-strip: "Batching, KV caching, quantization suggestions, and private deployment options."

SUPPORTING HERO ELEMENT (design notes):
- Include a compact badge row under the hero with 3 short chips (Latency SLOs • Dedicated GPU pools • Private VPC). Each chip opens a micro-modal with 1–2 sentences and a link to a product page.
- Keep hero visual minimal — use a small sequence diagram that shows request routing -> runtime -> fallback. Avoid heavy product screenshots in test.

PRODUCT PAGE SNIPPETS (short blocks for landing page sections)
Redwood Hosted (one-liner + 3 bullets):
- One-liner: "Get started in minutes with curated models and transparent performance profiles."
- Bullets: "Streaming + function calling, built-in rate limiting, usage analytics."

Redwood Dedicated (one-liner + 3 bullets):
- One-liner: "Reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation."
- Bullets: "SLA-backed latency targets, configurable autoscaling, burst capacity."

Redwood Private (one-liner + 3 bullets):
- One-liner: "Bring inference into your VPC or on-prem with audit logs and KMS/HSM integrations."
- Bullets: "Customer-managed keys, private control plane, air-gapped packaging available."

TECHNICAL REASSURANCE BLOCK (short, scannable)
- Latency SLOs: "Pick a 99th percentile latency SLO per-route; we surface violations to tracing and alerting."
- Graceful degradation: "Automatic fallback to verified compatible model variants when capacity or latency constraints occur."
- Responsible default policies: "Rate limits, adaptive batching, and token-level cost visibility enabled by default for new accounts."
- Security & governance: "Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM support, audit logs, and SOC-ready controls for Private deployments."
- Model provenance: "Model catalog entries include tokenizer, quantization profile, and performance trace for common request shapes."

COMPETITIVE NOTES (quick mental model for copy and objection handling)
- Generic cloud vendors (managed endpoints): often simple to start but lack production tooling for cost/latency controls. Emphasize: our runtime + routing policies + cost tooling.
- API-first providers (value simplicity): stronger onboarding but weaker enterprise controls. Emphasize: same developer ergonomics + enterprise features.
- Self-hosted runtimes (open-source stacks): powerful but operational burden. Emphasize: reduce ops cost, keep control with private deployment option.

OBJECTIONS & READY RESPONSES (for landing page micro-FAQ and sales snippets)
- "How do you guarantee latency?" -> "You can pin SLOs per route and reserve Dedicated capacity; we surface 99th percentile latency in the Console and include tracing hooks."
- "What happens during model overload?" -> "Requests are routed to compatible model variants or burst capacity; fallbacks are automatic and observable so you can tune policies."
- "Can we audit model use and keys?" -> "Yes — Private installs include audit logs and KMS/HSM integration; hosted customers get exportable audit trails."

HYPOTHESES (for A/B tests):
H1: Adding a single-line technical micro-strip under the CTA that references SLOs & fallbacks increases trial activation rate for engineering signups by +8–12%.
H2: Replacing marketing-y hero wording with an operations-focused hero (Variant B) increases click-to-try rate for visitors with engineering UA signals (tech docs, GitHub refs) by +15%.
H3: Adding hero chips with explainer modals decreases time-to-first-run among trial accounts by 20% (because they find relevant controls faster).

EXPERIMENT DESIGN / METRICS:
- Audience segmentation: All new visitors + targeted technical cohort (referrers: GitHub, dev.to, /r/MachineLearning).
- Primary metrics: trial activation (create key and call inference within 7 days), click-to-try, time-on-page, bounce rate.
- Secondary metrics: number of support tickets about "how to get predictable latency", NPS for trial accounts.
- Duration: 3 weeks per variant or until 3,000 unique visitors per variant.

ROLLOUT PLAN:
1) Implement small hero copy + micro-strip + chip row as opt-in variant in GA experiment framework (product-team to add micro-modal content).
2) Wire tracking: custom events (hero_cta_click, chip_modal_open, trial_api_call_first). Work with analytics to ensure funnel is tagged.
3) Run experiment for tech cohort and broad audience. Collect quantitative + open-text survey on success page for those who started a trial ("Was this info helpful? yes/no + why").
4) Debrief and iterate: if H1/H2 show lift, test combining micro-strip + chip modals and tune micro-copy.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs:
- Design: create a 2x2 micro-modal template (short title, single sentence, link to docs). Owner: Marcus. Due: 2025-03-05.
- Analytics: add events and segment filter for developer-referral domains. Owner: Sofia. Due: 2025-02-20.
- Legal/Compliance: short copy review for SLA wording. Owner: Ravi. Due: 2025-02-25.
- Engineering: confirm that fallback language maps to actual runtime behaviors (list of compatible model variants and how they are verified). Owner: Eng-serving-runtime owner TBD.

SAMPLE SALES ONE-LINERS (for chat widget / live demo):
- "We build fallbacks into the runtime so your product stays responsive even when models are busy — you can tune the downgrade policy per-route."
- "If you need full isolation, we support private VPC or on-prem with KMS/HSM and audit logs — common for regulated teams."

QUICK NOTE ON TONE: Keep hero terse and developer-respectful. Technical micro-strip should feel like a nod to engineers (short, actionable). Avoid marketing hyperbole — use concrete artifacts (SLOs, dedicated pools, fallback behavior).

FINAL REMARKS:
This brief is intentionally compact. The objective is a quick experiment that surfaces production assurances without creating marketing noise. We should prioritize fast iterations and measurement over a large rewrite.

END OF BRIEF

Feedback welcome — drop comments below or slack @ava.
